I've been farming these 4.5 mu for 25 years now. Last year my wheat did about 500 kg per mu, and the maize about 550 kg per mu. This year I'll do mostly the same — why change what works? My neighbor Lao Zhang had good results with the same seed and fertilizer, so I copy him.

For the wheat, I plant in October after running the rotary tiller. I buy improved wheat seed from the shop in town — about 15 kg per mu, so about 70 kg for the whole plot. I put down one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind. Then in spring when the wheat is turning green, I topdress with urea — about 35 kg per mu. Some people put more, but 35 kg has been enough for me, and fertilizer money is real money. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat survives the cold, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — herbicide when I plant, and once more if I see aphids or rust.

For the maize, right after I harvest wheat in June, I plant hybrid maize seed with the direct seeder. No need to plow — everyone here does no-tillage now. I use about 2 kg seed per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the ground with the planter, about 40 kg per mu. Then when the plants are knee-high at the big trumpet stage, I spread urea — about 30 kg per mu. I irrigate twice if the rain doesn't come: once when they're growing tall, once when the ears are filling. Two sprays — herbicide at the start, then something for armyworm if they show up.

My son works at the factory in town, so it's mostly me and my wife doing the field work. I have to watch every yuan. But I'd rather put a bit too much fertilizer than too little. A bad harvest means we dig into our savings. Waste some fertilizer? That's just a cost you accept. I expect 500 kg per mu for wheat and 550 kg per mu for maize if the weather holds. Last year was similar. I'll be happy with that.
